title: Derived constant/limit adjunction with its actual projection counit
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] admitting inverse limits of countable towers. Put $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system], with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Assume the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal T)$ exist [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and every complex in $\mathcal T$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal T)}(Z,I)=0$ for every acyclic $Z$. Let $L=\lim:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ and let $RL$ be its total right derived functor computed by $RL(QI)=Q(LI)$ on such resolutions. Let $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$ be the constant tower, also denoting its termwise exact derived functor by $\Delta$, and let $e_n:D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be evaluation. Define $\pi_{n,B}:RL(B)\to e_nB$ on a tower resolution $q:M\to I$ by the inverse-limit projection $LI\to I_n$ followed by $(Qq_n)^{-1}$, with the canonical resolution identifications. The ordinary adjunction $\Delta\dashv L$ induces a canonical adjunction $\Delta:D(\mathcal A)\rightleftarrows D(\mathcal T):RL$ whose counit $\epsilon_B:\Delta RL(B)\to B$ satisfies $e_n(\epsilon_B)=\pi_{n,B}$ under $e_n\Delta=\mathrm{id}$, naturally in $B$ and independently of its resolution. For any category $\mathcal J$, functors $C:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal A)$, $B:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal T)$, and natural transformation $\lambda:C\to RL\circ B$, the maps $\eta_j=\epsilon_{B_j}\circ\Delta(\lambda_j)$ form a natural transformation $\Delta C\to B$ in the derived tower category and satisfy $e_n\eta_j=\pi_{n,B_j}\lambda_j$.
